confounds: Diagnosed users have higher retained activity: approximately 620 versus 531 posts per user on average and 391 versus 334 at the median; word-normalized and per-user statistics reduce but do not eliminate exposure bias.

No timestamps or external clinical ground truth were available; timeline-level recurrence should not be interpreted as temporal persistence, episode duration, causality, or diagnosis.

negative_results: Generic negative, literal-death, negation, absolutist, positive-affect, and first-person-any indicators were near ceiling or context-contaminated; raw keywords alone were not persuasive.
Specific anhedonia-like language was rare: 13/619 diagnosed users (2.1%) versus 78/5463 controls (1.4%), a small +0.7 percentage-point difference.
Specific hopelessness templates were weak and inconsistent: 26.2% versus 20.8% overall, but the direction reversed in one of four folds.
Punctuation, capitalization, emoji, ellipsis, and quote-character rates did not provide stable standalone evidence.

Generic death vocabulary was inadequate for self-harm inference: literal-death language occurred in 72.7% of diagnosed users versus 65.3% of controls, but included idioms, fiction, news, humor, and third-person references.
Temporal persistence or episode duration could not be established from source-order timelines without timestamps.
